review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, regression design self-review
review.decision: Tie missing-proof alerts to live receiver acknowledgements after the grace period
review.notes: The production evidence identified a fresh acknowledgement at six seconds, a settled historical aggregate, and an independent archive addition. Use durable synthetic records, an explicit clock, and a fake desktop channel to reproduce the same transitions. The fixtures contain invented content.

cases.description: Fresh or settled receiver acknowledgements do not revive historical missing-proof alerts
cases.setup: Seed a historical accepted-unverified marker and its notice watermark, a successful later confirmation, a separately reported archive marker, and synthetic active receiver acknowledgements with a controlled clock.
cases.action: Run the real health watchdog while observation is empty, at six seconds after a fresh acceptance, and across the grace boundary. Leave one overdue receipt active while a different one ages, then retire each receipt and run the watchdog again.
cases.expected: A settled marker and a fresh receipt produce zero missing-proof journal or desktop alerts. A receipt reaching the grace period independently emits a missing-proof alert. A distinct later overdue receipt emits a new rate-limited alert even while the earlier one remains. Repeated scans send neither receipt again. After retirement there is no active missing-proof notice. A newly archived acknowledgement remains a separate alert.
